LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD is a conventional from-source AUR build. It clones the project's own upstream repository (`github.com/Vniverse77/MIGA.git`, tag `v0.4.0`) and drives the upstream build system: `npm install` + `npm run build:desktop` for the web frontend, then `npx tauri build --no-bundle` for the Rust/Tauri desktop binary. The `package()` function only copies the resulting binary, license, `.desktop` entry, and icon assets into `$pkgdir` under the expected `/usr` paths. No files are written or read outside the source tree and `$pkgdir`.

There is no obfuscation, no encoded/assembled command strings, no `eval`, no `curl | bash`, no `git pull`/`git fetch`+`reset --hard` in `build()` or `prepare()`, no post-install hook, and no attempt to read or transmit local data (SSH/GPG keys, `/etc/shadow`, environment variables, browser data). Nothing contacts a host unrelated to the package.

Hygiene notes only (not evidence of malice): `sha256sums=('SKIP')` is used on a VCS source, which is required practice for `git+` sources rather than a verification failure; `npm install` resolves dependencies from the npm registry at build time without a lockfile pin in the PKGBUILD itself, which widens the transitive supply-chain window; and the pinned `v$pkgver` tag is mutable (a tag can be re-pointed), so a commit hash would be more reproducible. These are best-practice concerns, not malicious behavior, and the application is self-described as an end-to-end encrypted messenger, so no telemetry or privacy concern is visible at the packaging layer.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard source build of upstream Tauri app; no malicious behavior.</summary>
</security_assessment>
